I also found exact constructions for register projection and for cancelling an unknown resistivity factor in a proposed velocity readout.

The remaining gap is physical and quantitative: **the proposed final conversion from magnetic registers to an arbitrary even velocity response lacks a polynomial stability estimate for arbitrary incoming errors and \(L^\infty_tL^2_x\) disturbances.** Its favorable Fourier structure controls the intended reference packets, but does not automatically control perturbations outside that structure.

Below I distinguish the exact reductions from the physical estimates that remain unproved. In particular, I do not interpret an exponential sufficient estimate for this construction as a negative answer to your existence question.

## 1. The target representation has polynomial bounds

Write \(\kappa=2\pi\), and use the coefficient norm
\[
\|F\|_{\mathcal X}
=
\sum_k(1+7|k|_1)
\bigl(|F_k^c|_1+|F_k^s|_1\bigr).
\]
Your promise is
\[
\sum_\alpha
\left(\|U_\alpha\|_{\mathcal X}
+\|Z_\alpha\|_{\mathcal X}\right)\le K.
\]

For \(|h|\le1\), every \(|h^\alpha|\le1\). Consequently, if spatial frequencies with \(|k|_\infty>N\) are discarded,
\[
\sup_{|h|\le1}
\left(
\|U(h)-U_N(h)\|_2+
\|Z(h)-Z_N(h)\|_2
\right)
\le \frac{K}{1+7N}.
\]
Thus a cutoff \(N=\lceil CK/\epsilon\rceil\), with a fixed sufficiently large \(C\), pays the spatial tail. There is no need to enumerate up to a large binary-encoded input frequency: one compares each listed frequency directly with \(N\).

The number of possible monomials is
\[
\#\{\alpha\in\mathbb N^3:|\alpha|\le D\}
=\binom{D+3}{3}.
\]
After truncation, the possible monomial–spatial-frequency keys therefore number
\[
O\!\left((D+1)^3(N+1)^3\right).
